title: NOx Sensor Circuit Bank 1
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the NOx sensor (bank 1), which measures nitrogen oxide pollution in diesel exhaust so the exhaust treatment system can adjust. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Faulty NOx sensor
Damaged, corroded or unplugged connector
Broken or chafed wiring
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the NOx sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the NOx sensor.

title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
plain: The NOx sensor (bank 1) is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor measures nitrogen oxide pollution in diesel exhaust so the exhaust treatment system can adjust. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration NOx sensor
A real fault in the system the sensor monitors
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the NOx sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the NOx sensor if its readings are off.

title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low Input Bank 1
plain: The signal from the NOx sensor (bank 1) is lower than the computer expects. This sensor measures nitrogen oxide pollution in diesel exhaust so the exhaust treatment system can adjust. A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground
Failed NOx sensor
Corroded or damaged connector
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the NOx sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the NOx sensor.

title: NOx Sensor Circuit High Input Bank 1
plain: The signal from the NOx sensor (bank 1) is higher than the computer expects. This sensor measures nitrogen oxide pollution in diesel exhaust so the exhaust treatment system can adjust. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Unplugged or corroded connector
Failed NOx sensor
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the NOx sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the NOx sensor.

title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent Input Bank 1
plain: The signal from the NOx sensor (bank 1) keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor measures nitrogen oxide pollution in diesel exhaust so the exhaust treatment system can adjust. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector
Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves
Failing NOx sensor

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the NOx sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the NOx sensor.

title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
plain: The engine computer can't properly control the NOx sensor heater (bank 1), which heats the NOx sensor so it can read accurately. It sees an open or broken circuit, often from wiring, a connector or the part itself.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Failed NOx sensor (heater is built in)
Broken wire or unplugged connector
Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the NOx sensor connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the NOx sensor (heater is built in).

title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1
plain: The control circuit for the NOx sensor heater (bank 1) is reading low voltage. This part heats the NOx sensor so it can read accurately. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible emissions warning or reduced power on some diesels

causes.name: Control wire shorted to ground
Internally shorted NOx sensor (heater is built in)
Damaged connector
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Check the NOx sensor wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the NOx sensor resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the NOx sensor (heater is built in).

fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the NOx sensor (heater is built in).

title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: Inside the oxygen sensor (bank 1, sensor 1) or its wiring, the signal wire is touching the heater wire. The computer can't trust the reading.

causes.name: Internally shorted oxygen sensor
Melted or chafed sensor wiring touching the exhaust
Water or corrosion in the sensor connector

checks: Inspect the O2 sensor wiring near the exhaust for melted spots
Unplug the sensor and check for a short between signal and heater pins
fix: Repair melted wiring if found; otherwise replace the oxygen sensor.
